political_impact.text: Restored to the public domain 120 acres adjoining Lawton that had been reserved in 1901 for the Fort Sill Indian boarding school, so the city could buy them for a park under the act of September 30, 1890.
The proclamation answered a request from Lawton's city authorities, who wanted to enter the land for park purposes.

related.note: Restored a forty-acre Fort Sill sub-agency tract to Lawton for a cemetery in 1902.
Freed agency land beside Anadarko for a town park in 1902.

uncertain: Whether Lawton ever completed the purchase and used the 120 acres as a park, and when it gave them up, has not been established; the area is now mapped as residential streets.
How Lawton's newspapers, or any others, reported the grant in 1904 has not been checked.

political_impact.text: Restored to the public domain the four-acre Court House Reserve, lot one of block forty-eight in the Woodward townsite, to be disposed of to the Town of Woodward for a public park under the Oklahoma townsite act of May 14, 1890.
The Woodward County commissioners had relinquished the lot and recommended that it be patented to the town for a park.

uncertain: Whether the Town of Woodward received a patent for the lot is not known, and the lot has not been located on a modern plat.
How Woodward's newspapers reported the grant in 1904 has not been checked.

political_impact.text: Of the forty proclamations printed in volume 33 of the Statutes at Large (March 1903 to March 1905), only these two restore a single small tract to a named town.
